feat(hooks): gate parens release-please rejects (#1268)

* feat(hooks): read whole commit message from argv

제목만 보던 공유 파서를 본문까지 읽도록 확장합니다. 릴리스가 조용히
커밋을 버리는 형태가 본문 줄에 살기 때문에, 제목 게이트가 쓰는 argv
워크로는 닿지 않습니다.

- git_commit_titles: argv 워크를 `_scan_commit_message_values` 로 한 번만
  돌게 묶고, extract_git_titles 와 새 extract_git_message_texts 가 그
  결과를 각자 읽습니다. 사본을 하나 더 만드는 것이 #594 이전 두 파서가
  드리프트한 경로라 워크는 계속 하나입니다.
- text_from_file: -F 파일의 전문. title_from_file 이 여기서 첫 줄을 뗍니다.
- _hook_utils.heredoc_bodies: strip_heredoc_bodies 의 짝. 힙독 본문은
  토크나이저가 지워버리므로 원문에서만 회수됩니다.

기존 두 제목 게이트의 판정은 그대로입니다 (format 66건, length 63건,
lib 52건 전부 통과).

Confidence: high
Not-tested: 게이트 두 개가 실제 세션에서 부르는 경로는 플러그인 캐시의
 이전 릴리스라, 이 변경의 런타임 동작은 워킹 트리 직접 실행으로만 확인

* feat(hooks): gate parens release-please rejects

release-please 가 쓰는 파서는 본문의 모든 줄을 `type(scope):` 헤더로
파싱합니다. 줄 첫머리의 공백 없는 낱말이 `(` 에 붙으면 그 괄호가 scope
로 열리고, 같은 줄에서 깨끗이 닫히지 않으면 커밋 전체가 거부됩니다.
거부된 커밋은 건너뛰어지는데 릴리스 워크플로는 그대로 success 로 끝나서,
CHANGELOG 항목만 조용히 사라집니다. 릴리스 2회분에서 3건이 그렇게
빠졌고 (#1228), 다음 릴리스는 직전 태그부터 계산하므로 복구되지 않습니다.

#1233 의 check-changelog-coverage 는 이 누락을 붉은불로 세우는 탐지기고,
이 게이트는 커밋이 아직 편집 가능한 유일한 시점에서 막는 예방기입니다.

판별 규칙은 실제 파서 0.4.1 에 물어서 고정했습니다. 통과 조건 네 가지 -
괄호 없음 또는 1열, 앞부분에 공백, 앞부분에 `!` 또는 `:`, 다른 괄호보다
먼저 닫힘 - 는 모두 측정된 PASS 이지 문법 추론이 아닙니다. 표는 spec 에
있습니다.

등급은 blocking (exit 2), PRAXIS_COMMIT_PAREN_STRICT=0 으로 advisory.
근거는 셋입니다. 이 저장소 전체 이력 659커밋에서 오탐 0 / 미탐 0 이고,
검사가 순수 로컬 문자열 연산이라 length-check 를 advisory 로 만든
네트워크 호출이 없으며, 오탐 비용은 공백 하나인 반면 미탐 비용은 복구
불가한 CHANGELOG 항목입니다. 같은 기계 소비자를 지키는 format-check 가
blocking 인 것과 같은 자리입니다.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: 실제 세션이 부르는 것은 플러그인 캐시의 이전 릴리스이므로,
 릴리스 이후 런타임에서 이 훅이 실제로 발화하는지는 미확인

* test(hooks): re-derive sibling gate count as 8

The manifest entry for commit-message-paren-check took the derived sibling
commit-gate list from 7 to 8, but the test oracle still pinned 7, the old
per-host counts, and the fixture anchors that quote the prose surfaces
verbatim. The expected values here are re-derived from hooks/manifest.json
directly, not copied from the checker under test.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: nothing beyond the suite itself — the oracle is a constant list.

* fix(hooks): strip <<- tabs from every body line

bash strips leading tabs from all of a `<<-` heredoc's input lines, not only
from the delimiter line. heredoc_bodies applied lstrip only to the terminator
comparison and returned the raw line, so commit-message-paren-check received
a body line the shell never produces: a real `word(a(b))` arrived as
`\tword(a(b))`, whose leading run holds whitespace, and the whitespace clause
skipped it.

Probe, bash 3.2.57(1)-release:

    $ printf 'cat <<-EOF\n\tword(a(b))\n\t\tindented\n\tEOF\n' > d3.sh
    $ bash d3.sh | od -c
    0000000   w o r d ( a ( b ) ) \n i n d e n t e d \n

The mirror test against strip_heredoc_bodies now compares lines with leading
tabs dropped on both sides: the property it pins is which lines are body, and
`<<-` makes the two sides disagree on a body line's text by design.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: bash versions other than 3.2.57 (macOS system bash) — the tab rule
is POSIX and unchanged in bash 5, but only 3.2.57 was executed here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XRSuj7p1m6R5hzLemNS7SR

* fix(hooks): bind heredoc reads to the source

The heredoc read was scoped to a `git commit` argv that produced no readable
message at all, which is the wrong condition in both directions.

Too narrow: `git commit -m 'fix: x' -m "$(cat <<'EOF' … EOF)"` resolves the
first `-m`, so the early return fired and the malformed body was never graded.
Too wide: with no resolvable source, every heredoc in the command was read, so
an unrelated `cat > notes <<'NOTE'` earlier in the chain blocked a commit whose
own message was clean.

Both shapes name their own heredoc. An unresolvable `-m` value carries the
opener inside its token (`$(cat <<'EOF'`), and `-F -` reads stdin from a
redirection on its own argv, so heredoc_bodies_by_delimiter plus
heredoc_delimiters bind each source to the body it opens. A delimiter word
reused by two heredocs identifies neither, and that source contributes nothing
rather than guessing.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: a `-F -` fed by a process substitution or a pipe rather than a
heredoc — it resolves to no delimiter and passes silently, same as before.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XRSuj7p1m6R5hzLemNS7SR

* fix(hooks): accept a path-prefixed git binary

_scan_commit_message_values compared argv[0] to the literal "git", so
`/usr/bin/git commit -m 'word(a(b))'` produced no message source and every
gate built on this walk went silent — the three commit gates that share it,
the new paren gate included. Mirror the _is_git_binary the sibling commit
gates already carry, which is the same path-prefix hole #1099 closed for gh.

A lookalike name is still not the binary: gitk, mygit and legit all fail the
check, and the tests pin both directions.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: a shell function or alias named git — a hook reading argv cannot
see either, and no sibling gate covers it.

* fix(hooks): inspect commits inside substitutions

main walked only the top-level command starts, and safe_tokenize coalesces a
`$( ... )` run into one token, so `MSG=$(git commit -m 'word(a(b))')` carried
no `git` argv[0] at any level the scan reached and the gate stayed silent.
iter_command_texts already yields the outer text plus the inner text of every
ACTIVE substitution, which is the surface the sibling gates from #1032/#1035
use; quoting still decides what is active, so a `$(git commit ...)` printed
from inside single quotes is text and is not graded.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: substitutions nested deeper than MAX_SUBST_DEPTH (4) — the shared
helper stops there and this hook inherits that bound.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XRSuj7p1m6R5hzLemNS7SR

* fix(hooks): blank a later-line substitution

Only line 0 of a multi-line `-m` value decided whether the value was
knowable, so `-m "fix: x\n\n$(git log --oneline"` passed the rest through as
message text. The shell replaces that line with a command's output, but the
body gate saw raw shell text whose leading word is glued to `(` and blocked a
message nobody can predict.

Each line is now tested on its own and an unknowable one is blanked rather
than dropped, so the line number the gate reports still points at the real
message. The single-quote exception matches a whole quoted run by value, so it
cannot reach a line of a multi-line run: a literal `$(...)` line inside a
single-quoted message is blanked too. That is a false negative, which is the
fail-open direction, and it is pinned by test.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: a message whose later line opens a backtick substitution spanning
into the next line — the per-line test reads one line at a time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XRSuj7p1m6R5hzLemNS7SR

* perf(hooks): read one line for a commit title

title_from_file took the first line off text_from_file's whole-file `.read()`,
so the two pre-existing title gates paid for the entire `-F` file to answer a
question about its first 50 characters. A `-F` path is arbitrary and both
gates run on every `git commit` a session makes.

Measured, mean of 20 calls per file, same machine:

    file     BEFORE (.read())   AFTER (readline)
    500 B           0.066 ms           0.078 ms
    1 MB            0.718 ms           0.041 ms
    50 MB          47.016 ms           0.023 ms

The 500 B row is the cost of the change: one extra buffered read call, and it
is noise. The body gate still needs every line and keeps calling
text_from_file. Path resolution moved into a shared helper so the two readers
cannot drift on where `-` and a relative path go.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: nothing behavioural — the two readers were compared on a trailing
newline, CRLF, an empty file, an empty first line, and a non-UTF-8 file, all
pinned by test.

* ci: fetch full history for the test job

The paren gate's fixtures are the real commits release-please rejected,
read back with `git log -1 --format=%B <sha>`. actions/checkout defaults
to a shallow clone, so those objects are absent on CI and both fixture
tests error with exit 128 rather than asserting anything. The repo
already uses fetch-depth:0 for gitleaks, and at 657 commits the full
history costs little.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: verified by reading the failing CI log and the checkout
default; the fix itself is confirmed only by the next CI run.

* fix(hooks): skip a line an expansion rewrites

The gate graded the source text of a message value instead of the text
bash delivers to git, so two shapes blocked commits that are valid.

A substitution was treated as unreadable only when it OPENED the line, so
`foo($(printf x))` was graded raw and read as a nested paren; git receives
`foo(x)`, which release-please parses. Position does not decide whether a
line is readable, so `has_shell_expansion` does, and it covers parameter
expansion too.

An unterminated `$(` made the gate blank that one line and grade the rest
as message text. Bash never finishes parsing such a command, so no commit
happens at all and the following lines are the inside of an unfinished
substitution rather than message lines. Measured:

  $ bash -c 'git commit -m "fix: x\n\n$(x\n\nword(a(b))"'
  bash: -c: line 5: syntax error: unexpected end of file

A whole value that arrived as one single-quoted run is now graded verbatim
rather than line-blanked: the shell substitutes nothing inside it, which
also removes the false negative the by-value match used to carry.

Every expectation was measured before it was asserted, by running the
command under bash with git replaced by a recorder that prints the argv
and the message it was handed.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: shlex has already stripped quoting from a value, so an escaped
  `\$` cannot be told from a live one and its line is blanked — a false
  negative, pinned by test rather than closed.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XRSuj7p1m6R5hzLemNS7SR

* fix(hooks): bind a heredoc to the text bash feeds

Five shapes disagreed with what the reading command actually receives.

A spaced `<< EOF` puts the operator and the delimiter in separate tokens,
and the scan applied its per-token reader to each one, so a stdin heredoc
feeding `git commit -F -` named no delimiter and was never read.

Redirections apply left to right, so `cat <<A <<B` reads B and discards A.
Every delimiter a source opened was collected, so malformed prose in the
discarded body blocked a commit whose real message is clean.

A backtick run re-enters shell parsing inside double quotes exactly as
`$(…)` does, so the `<<EOF` in it opens a heredoc. Reading it as string
data let a malformed message pass unseen.

An unquoted delimiter leaves the body subject to expansion, so the raw
lines are not the delivered ones. The body is now spliced and its
expansion-carrying lines blanked before grading. Measured:

  $ bash -c 'git commit -m "$(cat <<-EOF ... `(a(b))` note ... EOF)"'
  bash: command substitution: line 0: syntax error near unexpected token
  {"argv": ["commit", "-m", "fix: x\n\n note"]}

A backslash-newline is removed by bash, not turned into a separator, so
splicing it to a space produced a word no longer glued to its paren — the
one shape this gate always passes. Splicing is skipped inside a
single-quoted run and inside heredoc bodies, where bash does not splice
either, and where joining lines would move every line number after it.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: a delimiter word that names two heredocs still identifies
  neither, so that source contributes no text — unchanged fail-open.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XRSuj7p1m6R5hzLemNS7SR

* fix(hooks): read git's short-option cluster grammar

Three branches covered a subset of one grammar, so the shapes between them
were either invisible or invented.

A cluster is leading no-value flags followed by at most one value-taking
flag, which consumes the rest of the cluster or, when the cluster ends with
it, the next token. The old rule required the token to END in `m`, so
`-am"fix: x"` yielded no message source at all, and `-F` was recognised only
detached, so `-Fmsg.txt` and `-F-` named no file. One walk now covers
`-mvalue`, `-am value`, `-am"value"`, `-vsm`, `-Ffile`, `-F-` and `-aF -`.

The whitelist that rejects `-Smike@example.com` is kept and now guards the
whole walk: an unknown character abandons the cluster rather than scanning
past it, so no message source is invented for a flag whose value shape this
module does not know.

Everything after `--` is a pathspec. The scan continued past it, so a path
literally named `-m` became a message source and its neighbour could block
a valid commit. Measured before and after:

  rc=2 <- git commit -m 'fix: x' -- '-m' 'word(a(b))'   (must be rc=0)
  rc=2 <- git commit -m 'fix: x' -m 'word(a(b))'        (control, correct)

The false-positive fixes land first on purpose: widening the set of
recognised sources before them would have exposed more commits to the
mis-grading they close.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: `-C`, `-c`, `-t` and `-u` take values this module does not read,
  so a cluster containing one contributes nothing rather than resolving it.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XRSuj7p1m6R5hzLemNS7SR

* docs(hooks): record the measured message surface

The source table listed the shapes the gate happened to handle. It now
lists the shapes git actually accepts, with the reading each one gets:
attached and clustered short options, the `--` pathspec separator, the
delimiter spellings, backtick substitutions, and the three cases whose
delivered text cannot be known and are therefore passed rather than graded.

Also records that each row was measured by running the command under bash
with git replaced by a recorder, rather than reasoned from the grammar, and
names the third heredoc-binding failure mode: grading a body that a later
redirection on the same source discards.

`heredoc_bodies_by_delimiter` is now `heredoc_sources`, which carries the
delimiter's quoting alongside the body.

Confidence: high
Not-tested: documentation only, no runtime behaviour.
